purpose: Real microbenchmark on RunPod community RTX 3090 24GB ($0.22/hr) to give independent measurements for the sim's calibration constants. Run 2026-05-11.

h2d_bandwidth.description: Time for `tensor.to('cuda')` on pinned uint8 tensors. 5 reps each after one warmup. Variance is sub-1% for all sizes — H2D is highly deterministic.

samples_gb_17.note: Higher effective bandwidth at large sizes — DMA chunking / driver-level optimization kicks in.

sd15_inference.description: Stable Diffusion v1-5 (public-license) 1024x1024 20-step inference on RTX 3090. 5 reps after one warmup. SD-1.5 ~5GB FP16 used as a stand-in for SD3 17GB — same pipeline machinery, smaller weights, runs on 24GB card. RTX 3090 PCIe Gen3 is ~4× slower H2D than H100 SXM PCIe Gen5; inference time is hardware-bound but the variance (jitter) we measure here is what the sim was implicitly assuming = 0.

T_BIND_COLD_L2_validation.narrative: Pure H2D copy of 17 GB on RTX 3090 = 727 ms; on H100 SXM PCIe Gen5 it would be ~270 ms theoretically. The 2026-05-06 measurement of 1.04 s on H100 SXM has ~770 ms of non-H2D overhead (per-tensor cudaMemcpyAsync launch overhead — this matches the BPS failure post-mortem in commit cebd01d). Sim's 1.0 s is therefore well-calibrated for the **full bind path**, not just bandwidth.

T_INFER_validation.narrative: Different model + different GPU, so absolute values cannot be compared directly. SD-1.5 1024² on RTX 3090 vs SD3 1024² on H100 SXM 4-GPU: SD3 has ~4× the parameter count + does 3 text encoders, but H100 SXM 4-GPU has ~8× the FLOPs and uses sequence-parallel. Net wash, both ~3-4s. The key sim assumption being validated is **inference jitter ≈ 0**: real measurement gives 0.29% relative stdev (5 reps, ±13ms on 4.4s), which is empirically zero.

interpretation_for_sim_calibration.key_finding: Sim's constants are not overstated. The 2026-05-06 H100 SXM number for T_BIND_COLD_L2 (1.04 s) is consistent with the RTX 3090 H2D measurement (727 ms) plus the known per-tensor launch overhead in PyTorch's .to(). The sim's zero-jitter assumption for inference is empirically valid (real stdev/mean = 0.3%).
